page.title: Virtual Event Checklist Essentials
page.description: A practical checklist covering registration, engagement, recording, follow‑up and workstream ownership for virtual events, webinars and hybrid conferences.
page.h1: What belongs on a virtual event checklist?
page.definition: A virtual event checklist is a structured list of tasks, owners and deadlines that covers registration setup, audience engagement tools, live production details, recording delivery and post‑event follow‑up so nothing is missed from planning through replay distribution across all time zones and platforms.
page.quick_answer: Start with a master spreadsheet that assigns every task to a named owner and sets a due date; run a full rehearsal on the actual platform two to five days before go‑live.

sections.h2: What registration steps belong on a virtual event checklist?

blocks.p: Registration must capture attendee data, confirm capacity limits and trigger automated confirmations. Build a registration page that collects name, email, company and role, enforce a hard cap that matches the platform licence, and connect the form to an email sequence that sends a calendar invite and a reminder one day before the event.

ul: Capacity guard tied to platform licence

sections.h2: Which engagement tools should be planned for a virtual event?

blocks.p: Engagement tools need a live chat, poll, Q&A and a moderation workflow that routes questions to speakers in real time. Choose a platform that bundles chat, polls and Q&A, assign a moderator to triage incoming questions, and prepare pre‑written poll questions that align with each session topic.

ul: Speaker cue cards for answered questions

sections.h2: How should recording and replay delivery be handled?

blocks.p: Record the stream on the platform and a backup encoder, then edit and publish the replay within 24 to 48 hours. Enable cloud recording on the platform, run a simultaneous local capture via an encoder, and assign an editor to trim dead air, add lower thirds and export a high‑resolution MP4.

sections.h2: What follow‑up actions close the loop after a virtual event?

blocks.p: Follow‑up includes sending the replay, a short survey, lead scoring and a sales hand‑off within one business day. Attach the replay link in a thank‑you email, embed a three‑question survey, push attendance data into the CRM for scoring, and notify the assigned sales rep with a summary of engaged accounts.

sections.h2: Which workstreams and owners keep a virtual event on track?

blocks.p: Eight workstreams each with a single owner cover intake, brief, production, review, approval, publishing, reporting and archive. Assign a project lead for intake, a content strategist for brief, a producer for production, an editor for review, a stakeholder for approval, a publisher for publishing, an analyst for reporting and an archivist for archive. West Peek Productions produces virtual, hybrid and webinar events and sets up marketing, content and creative operations.

faq.q: How far in advance should I lock the platform and venue AV for a hybrid conference?
faq.a: Lock the platform and venue AV six to eight weeks before the event, before the agenda is final, to allow time for speaker rehearsals and backup stream testing. This lead time also covers contract review, technical run‑throughs and contingency planning for network failures.

faq.q: What is the typical cost range for a produced moderated webinar?
faq.a: A moderated webinar production typically costs two thousand five hundred to seven thousand five hundred dollars per event, covering a live producer, Q&A moderation, branded graphics and a backup stream. The fee also includes post‑event editing and short clip creation for social distribution.

faq.q: Which tools help manage the event calendar and task ownership?
faq.a: Common tools for the calendar and task ownership are Asana, Monday.com or Airtable for planning; Google Docs or Notion for briefs; and HubSpot or Salesforce for follow‑up tracking. These platforms let you assign owners, set due dates and surface dependencies across the eight workstreams.

faq.q: When should the replay be sent to attendees?
faq.a: Send the replay within 24 to 48 hours after the live session while the content is still fresh, and include a short highlight reel for quick consumption. Attach a feedback survey link and a clear call to action for the next event or product demo.
